rule: Oklahoma's state races on the November 3, 2026 ballot, keyed by the race ids in ballot_local_2026.sqlite, by the same rule as the Congress pages (ballot/polls/polls_2026.json) and Minnesota's file (polls_mn_state_2026.json). Polls only from pollsters in AAPOR's Transparency Initiative (John, 2026-09-29): the latest from up to five of them, and our own average of the ten most recent, the arithmetic shown. Each poll's figures are checked against the pollster's own release; a list of polls (Wikipedia's, labelled as secondary) is used only to find them and to count the polls left out.
note: No pollster in AAPOR's Transparency Initiative has published a poll of any Oklahoma state race in 2026, so no race has a poll to show. Every poll found was by a firm outside the Initiative, nearly all of them of the Republican primaries and runoffs; the only polls of a November matchup are Cole Hargrave Snodgrass & Associates' August 3-6 survey of the Lieutenant Governor's and Attorney General's races. ActiVote's list of state polls could not be found from its home page (2026-10-03) and was not read.

pollsters: Cole Hargrave Snodgrass & Associates (five: the Republican primary on February 10-15, May 5-9 and August 4-10, 2025 and January 26-30, 2026, and the Republican runoff on August 2-4, 2026)
Pulse Decision Science (four, for Club for Growth: the Republican primary on April 7-9 and May 26-28, 2026, and the runoff on June 21-23 and August 2-4, 2026)
Stratus Intelligence (two, the Republican primary, September and October 2025, for Charles McCall's campaign)
NonDoc Media and the Oklahoma Association of Broadcasters (the Republican primary, May 21-25, 2026, registered Republicans)
yes. every kid. (the Republican primary, October 29-31, 2025; the group's own poll)
Victory Insights (the Republican primary, February 23-25, 2025, for the Calvin Coolidge Project)
left_out.note: Governor. Nobody has published a poll of November's contest between Mike Mazzei and Cyndi Munson: Wikipedia's page has no general-election polling section (read 2026-10-03), 270toWin's Oklahoma governor page lists only primary and runoff polls, and every poll found asked about the Republican nomination, settled in the August 25 runoff. The count is of separate surveys: 13 of the June 16 primary and 4 of the runoff; Wikipedia's extra table of primaries with Ryan Walters (who did not run) repeats Cole Hargrave Snodgrass surveys, one of which (May 5-9, 2025) appears only there. None of the nine pollsters is on AAPOR's list of Transparency Initiative members. Emerson College Polling's own site search for Oklahoma lists no release after its 2023 approval poll (read 2026-10-03).
